title: Apartment mortgage down payment: the real scale from 5% to 40%
seoTitle: Mortgage down payment: how much money you need
description: Apartment mortgage down payment: 5% through Noua Casa, 15% standard, 25% in foreign currency. Complete scale and extra money needed.
descriptionLlm: Learn everything about apartment mortgage down payments in 2026: NBR rules, Noua Casa, developer down payments, and exact calculations for your budget.
keywords: avans apartament credit ipotecar, avans minim credit ipotecar, avans Noua Casă, costuri credit ipotecar, avans prima locuință
lead: When you start calculating an apartment mortgage down payment, the first number that comes to mind is 15%. However, this percentage is valid for a single case, your first home purchased with a lei denominated loan; otherwise, the bank adjusts it up or down depending on the program you apply for, the currency you borrow in, and how many homes you already own. Moreover, you will walk out of your pocket with more than just the down payment, no matter where you are on the scale. Below you have the complete scale, what current bank practices and state program conditions look like, plus the extra money besides the down payment that no one tells you about until you reach the notary with your paperwork.

sections.h2: The bank risk comes before your percentage

blocks.x: NBR rules form the basis of the down payment: the bank must remain below a certain financing degree, and you must enter the property with your own funds, because the risk of default decreases when you also have something to lose. Up to this point, all banks think alike. The difference appears at the final percentage, because the bank calculates it by taking into account the currency you borrow in, the type of property you purchase, how many properties you have in the background, the loan term, the interest rate you choose, the program you apply for, and what your income looks like.

This is how the same person, with the exact same apartment in front of them, can receive a lower down payment at one bank and a higher one at the competing bank. The figures above show current practice, because thresholds can shift from one period to another.

sections.h2: First home in lei starts at 15%

blocks.x: As long as you are buying your first home and borrowing in lei, major banks, from BCR, BT, and ING to Raiffeisen, UniCredit, BRD, and CEC, require from 15% of the property value. For a 100,000 euro apartment, this means 15,000 euro from your funds, while the loan covers 85,000 euro.

Since the threshold depends on each bank practice and can shift, you should confirm it with the bank before building your payment plan around it. Furthermore, the complete journey, from the application file to the signature, is explained in the mortgage credit guide.

If you borrow in euro, the bank starts at 25%, regardless of whether the apartment is your first one. The same threshold comes into play when you already own a home, whether you finished paying for the first one or are still paying installments. And if the collateral is intravital land, the down payment starts from 40%.

There are also loans that cover 100% of the value, without a down payment, but they come with a heavy condition: you must bring a second property into the bank collateral, in addition to the home you are buying. For a loan taken by two people, when one of the spouses owns a property, banks split paths: some demand 25% without discussion, while others settle for 15%.
The difference is directly visible in your account for the same 100,000 euro apartment: 15,000 euro out of pocket on the 15% threshold, and 25,000 euro on the 25% one.

sections.h2: The state lowers the down payment to 5%, not the bank

blocks.x: Noua Casa, the name adopted in 2020 by the former Prima Casa under the same FNGCIMM mechanism, lowers the down payment to 5% for homes up to 70,000 euro and keeps it at 15% for new or consolidated homes up to 140,000 euro. The ceilings, as of September 9, 2026, are as follows: 70,000 euro for an existing home and 140,000 euro for a new one, for building a house, and for an energy efficient home, while the state guarantee covers 50 to 60% of the loan.

The difference is visible on a 70,000 euro home: a 3,500 euro down payment through the program, 10,500 euro for the standard loan, and 17,500 euro if you reached the 25% threshold. We were talking about 7,000 to 14,000 euro remaining in your account when you qualify for the program. From the apartment prices page, you can quickly find out if the home you have in mind falls below the ceiling.

sections.h2: Once in a lifetime, with strict conditions

blocks.x: The basic condition states that you must not own any home, or you must own at most one with a usable area below 50 square meters, purchased outside the program. You can access it only once in a lifetime, you need Romanian citizenship or permanent residency, and the bank will not approve your loan if the installment plus the monthly reserve exceed 45% of your income. The purchased home becomes your primary residence, and the interest rate stays below a ceiling built on IRCC, with a bank margin of at most 2%; you can find out the exact figure at the bank upon your loan request.

sections.h2: Besides the down payment, another 3 to 5% of the home value comes out

blocks.x: The bank finances your apartment, while the surrounding expenses remain your responsibility. At the notary, you pay 1 to 2% of the property value, and for a 100,000 euro apartment, this means 1,000 to 2,000 euro just for paperwork. The evaluator sent by the bank charges 300 to 800 lei, and mandatory insurances, from PAD to home and life insurance, add another 200 to 300 lei per year.

With the whole package, the starting sum climbs 3 to 5% above the down payment: besides the 15,000 euro for the 100,000 euro apartment, you should prepare another 3,000 to 5,000 euro, plus a reserve for the month when an income payment is delayed.

faq.q: How much money should I prepare for a 100,000 euro apartment?
faq.a: For a standard lei credit for your first home, you start with a 15,000 euro down payment. Besides the 15,000, the notary takes 1,000 to 2,000 euro, the evaluator 300 to 800 lei, and insurances require another 200 to 300 lei per year, so the total entry amount reaches around 18,000 to 20,000 euro. Through the state program, for a 70,000 euro home, the down payment drops to 3,500 euro; for a new 140,000 euro home, you stay at 15%, meaning 21,000 euro.

faq.q: Can I buy without any down payment?
faq.a: Only if you bring a second property into the bank collateral, in addition to the home you are purchasing.

faq.q: Why was I asked for 25% if my friend bought with 15%?
faq.a: Because the percentage is calibrated to you, not to the apartment itself: the loan currency, the fact that you own another home, the nature of the collateral, the program you apply for, or your income profile shifts the threshold. The same property can receive different percentages at two banks, so it is worth asking a second bank before stopping at the first refusal.
